problem: "ERM and LRA units often run at 100 Hz to 300 Hz with amplitudes of a few µm to hundreds of µm, and update at about 1 kHz" can be read as saying the motor itself responds at 1 kHz. An ERM cannot follow amplitude commands that fast; 1 kHz is the rate of the rendering/control loop, and the mechanical bandwidth of an ERM is far lower (tens of hertz).
fix: "The rendering loop that drives them often runs at about 1 kHz, but the actuator itself responds much more slowly; an ERM follows amplitude changes only up to a few tens of hertz."

problem: "a lateral force of a few mN" understates friction-modulated touchscreens and is vague; readers may think a touchscreen can only produce a barely noticeable push.
fix: Give a range instead: friction-modulated screens produce lateral forces of the order of tens of millinewtons, and vibration-based screens move the glass by a few micrometres.

problem: The "Typical maximum" column mixes units (N, N·m, m, mN, °C) and contains the word "large" for the motion platform, so the column cannot be compared or used in a numerical question.
fix: Put the unit and a number in each cell, for example "3 N to 4 N", "0.1 N·m to 1 N·m", "hundreds of N", "fractions of a metre" (or "travel of metres"), "mN range", "mN per pin", "a few °C".
